chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked, 'What should I do when I go out with the funeral procession, walking in front of it, or behind it, or to its right, or to its left?' So he said: 'If he (the deceased) was an opponent (of the Ahl al-Bayt), do not walk in front of him, for the Angels of Punishment will be facing him with the varieties of Punishment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for walking in front of a funeral procession if the deceased was an opponent of the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the spatial etiquette of following a funeral procession, specifically distinguishing between the deceased's spiritual status and the position of the mourners. He advises against walking in front of the coffin if the deceased was an opponent of the Ahl al-Bayt, as the 'Angels of Punishment' will be facing the deceased with various forms of retribution, a concept rooted in Shia eschatological tradition regarding the visibility of divine judgment during the journey of the soul.
